answer: Each identity registers one lagoon station and locks a 65 bond, filing a marble-tagged vial whose hash binds its key and one relic sample in the lagoon archive. Auditors check each vial against the relic reference and location; reuse, a wrong location, or a second key claiming the same sample burns the bond. The kth station pays 18+5(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 5,013 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,515,500 plus 65,000 locked. A rented-sample ring fails: one vial hash cannot support two keys. An honest sampler pays 18 once for one station and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
